 Coimbatore School Holiday Announced as Flooding Disrupts City
 By UrbanAcres Editorial 
 October 25, 2026 
 0 
 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp 
 Schools in Coimbatore and Dindigul will remain closed on October 26 as heavy rain affects Tamil Nadu, while schools and colleges in Puducherry and Karaikal will also observe a holiday, according to announcements cited by Dinamalar. The decision follows flooding in parts of Coimbatore and a weather warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rain in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
 The holiday in Coimbatore and Dindigul was announced by the respective district collectors as a precautionary measure. In Puducherry and Karaikal, Education Minister A. Namassivayam announced a holiday for both schools and colleges, the report said.
 The rain has disrupted normal life in several parts of Tamil Nadu. Key areas of Coimbatore have reportedly experienced flooding, with underground passages filled with water and motorists facing difficulty while travelling through affected stretches.
 The weather system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified, and the northeast monsoon has also become active, according to the report. The India Meteorological Department has warned of very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. The warning has raised concerns for school transport, pedestrian movement and access through low-lying roads and underpasses.
 The closure applies only to schools in Coimbatore and Dindigul, while the Puducherry and Karaikal announcement covers schools and colleges. The separate orders reflect decisions taken by local administrations in response to rainfall conditions in their respective jurisdictions.
 For families, the immediate operational issue is whether roads, bus routes and pedestrian crossings remain usable during the morning commute. Waterlogged underground passages can force vehicles and pedestrians to seek alternative routes, increasing travel disruption even where schools themselves are not affected.
 The school holiday announcements are precautionary administrative measures and do not indicate a closure of all public or private offices. Residents are expected to follow further instructions issued by district administrations and local authorities as weather conditions develop.
 The closures will take effect on October 26. Further decisions on educational institutions will depend on weather conditions and announcements from the concerned district administrations and the Puducherry government.
